sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Khichri is an example of ______ method of enhancement. (ii) Milk polybags should not be exposed to sunlight as vitamin ______ gets lost. (iii) Quality of oil becomes ______ when it is reheated repeatedly. (iv) During frying, the temperature of oil becomes ______ degrees C.

State True or False: (i) Pressure cooking kills all bacteria. (ii) During steaming, food does not come in direct contact with water. (iii) Cooking with solar energy is an environment-friendly method. (iv) Boiling is not a safe cooking method.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – boiling is a safe and simple method.

questions.q: Match the columns: (i) Grill bars (ii) Oven (iii) Kadahi (iv) Tava; (A) Pastry (B) Chapatti (C) Kababs (D) Pakoras.

State True or False: (i) Boiled food can be made palatable by adding lemon or spices. (ii) Stewing is done below the boiling point. (iii) The lid should be tightly closed while steaming food. (iv) A solar cooker does not produce any smoke.

Match the food with the method of enhancement: (I) Dosa (II) Dhokla (III) Sprouted moong dal chaat (IV) Wheat besan ladoo; (a) Combination (b) Combination and fermentation (c) Fermentation (d) Germination.

Fill in the blanks: (i) Cooking in a closed oven is called ______. (ii) Cooking directly on hot sand or tava is ______. (iii) Cooking in hot oil is ______. (iv) In ______ the temperature used is as high as 200–300 degrees C.
questions.answer: (i) baking. (ii) roasting. (iii) frying. (iv) dry heat cooking.

questions.q: Arrange the steps in the correct order to conserve nutrients: (a) watch the time while cooking (b) wash the vegetables (c) cook in a covered pan (d) peel the vegetables thinly (e) cut the vegetables into big pieces.
questions.answer: (b) wash the vegetables; (d) peel thinly; (e) cut into big pieces; (c) cook in a covered pan; (a) watch the time.

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Cooking soda has no harmful effect on the nutrients of food. (ii) Minerals are lost when the cooking water is thrown away. (iii) Maximum loss of nutrients occurs in pressure cooking. (iv) Vitamin C is easily destroyed during cooking.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Write two differences between steaming and boiling methods of cooking.
questions.answer: In steaming the food does not touch water and is cooked by the heat of water vapour; in boiling the food is cooked in water. Steaming conserves nutrients, colour and flavour better, while in boiling water-soluble nutrients are lost if the water is thrown away.

or.q: Give two advantages of including germinated foods in the meals.
or.answer: Germination increases digestibility because some carbohydrates and proteins break into simpler forms, and it raises the nutritive value (vitamins) at no extra cost.

questions.q: Write two differences between boiling and pressure cooking methods.
questions.answer: Boiling is done at 100 degrees C in an open pan with plenty of water and takes longer; pressure cooking is done above 100 degrees C in steam under pressure, takes about one-third of the time, saves fuel and needs little water. Pressure cooking kills all bacteria and loses less water-soluble vitamins.

questions.q: Mention any four reasons by which nutrients get destroyed while cooking vegetables.
questions.answer: Cutting into small pieces and washing after cutting; discarding the cooking water; using cooking soda; overcooking or cooking in an uncovered pan; deep frying at very high temperature; leaving cut vegetables exposed to air for long.

questions.q: Give four suggestions to conserve nutrients while cooking vegetables.
questions.answer: Wash before cutting; scrape peels thin; cut into big pieces just before cooking; use just enough water and use the extra water; do not add soda; cook in a covered pan; do not overcook (any four).

or.q: State four reasons nutrients of pulses might get destroyed while cooking.
or.answer: Soaking and cooking in a lot of water that is thrown away (vitamin B lost); adding cooking soda; overcooking; cooking in an open pan for long; adding acids early which toughens protein.

questions.q: Write any four reasons for cooking food.
questions.answer: It makes food easy to digest; improves appearance, flavour, colour, texture and taste; adds variety; helps food to keep longer; makes food safe by killing harmful micro-organisms.

questions.q: Write two advantages of the roasting method and two drawbacks of the deep frying method.
questions.answer: Roasting: food becomes tastier and a variety is added to the meal. Deep frying: fried food is difficult to digest; it is high in calories and excess intake is bad for health.

questions.q: Name the two fastest methods of cooking and write two drawbacks of a solar cooker.
questions.answer: Pressure cooking and microwave cooking are the fastest. A solar cooker works only when there is plenty of sunshine and can only be used outdoors.

questions.q: Why is vitamin A lost when spinach is deep fried?
questions.answer: Vitamin A is fat-soluble and oxidised in contact with air; the temperature of deep frying (about 300 degrees C) destroys it rapidly. Cooking in a covered pan prevents its loss.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Analyse any six reasons why nutrients of potatoes and methi are lost while cooking them.
questions.answer: Potatoes: peeling thickly removes minerals and vitamins just under the skin; cutting into small pieces; washing after cutting; boiling in a lot of water and discarding it (vitamin C, B and minerals); overcooking; frying at high temperature. Methi: cutting fine and washing after cutting; cooking in an open pan (vitamin A is oxidised and vitamin C is lost); deep frying (about 300 degrees C destroys vitamin A); using soda; long cooking.

questions.q: Briefly explain any three methods of cooking food by dry heat.
questions.answer: Baking: food is cooked by hot air in a closed heated box, the oven (bread, cake, biscuits). Roasting: food is put directly on a hot tava, sand or fire and turned (brinjal, maize, groundnuts). Grilling: food is cooked on an iron grid over a glowing fire or between heated bars, more slowly than roasting (kababs, bati).

questions.q: How are foods combined, fermented and germinated? State their advantages.
questions.answer: Combination: foods of different groups are eaten together or in one dish (khichri, missi roti); the protein quality improves without extra cost. Fermentation: micro-organisms from curd or yeast act on batter or dough (idli, dhokla); nutrients become simpler, vitamins B and C are formed and the food becomes soft and digestible. Germination: grains are soaked 8–16 hours and sprouted 12–24 hours in a moist cloth; digestibility and nutritive value increase at no extra cost.

questions.q: Your mother is cooking chapatti, dal and vegetables for lunch. Give one suggestion each to enhance the nutritive value of each dish.
questions.answer: Chapatti: mix pulses or soya flour or add grated vegetables (missi roti, methi paratha) to improve proteins and vitamins. Dal: add spinach, moong or other vegetables, or combine with rice (khichri), and cook in a covered pan without soda. Vegetable: cut into large pieces just before cooking, cook in a covered pan with little water and use the water.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Give any five suggestions to conserve nutrients while preparing and cooking food.
questions.answer: (1) Wash vegetables before cutting, only as much as needed. (2) Scrape peels as thin as possible. (3) Cut into large pieces just before cooking. (4) Put vegetables into boiling water and use just enough water. (5) Use the extra water for soup or gravy. (6) Do not use cooking soda; a little lemon or tamarind helps keep vitamins. (7) Cook in a pan with a well-fitting lid and do not overcook.

questions.q: Describe boiling, steaming and pressure cooking with one advantage of each.
questions.answer: Boiling: food is cooked in an adequate quantity of water; it is safe and simple. Steaming: food is cooked by the heat of water vapour in a steamer (idli, dhokla); it conserves nutrients, colour and flavour and the food is light and easily digested. Pressure cooking: food is cooked in steam under pressure above 100 degrees C; it needs only about one-third of the time, saves fuel and kills all bacteria.
